conditions_text: Indian passport holders who also hold a valid US visa or Green Card (or a UK/EU residence visa) can get a UAE visa on arrival. The document must have at least 6 months' validity remaining.
fee_notes: Free on arrival under this route; one extension of 14 days available for a fee (AED 250).

conditions_text: Without a qualifying US/UK/EU (or Australia/Canada/Japan/South Korea/Singapore/New Zealand residence) document, Indian passport holders must arrange a UAE visa in advance.
Indian nationals holding a valid US, UK, Irish, or Schengen visa or residence permit are eligible for Turkey's e-Visa, single entry, applied for online.
fee_notes: Paid e-visa, applied for online in advance.

conditions_text: Turkey does not offer visa on arrival for Indian passport holders. Without a qualifying US/UK/Irish/Schengen visa, a sticker visa from a Turkish mission is required.
Indian nationals holding a valid US visa or permanent residence (Green Card) can enter Mexico for tourism without a separate Mexican visa. The FMM tourist permit is completed on arrival.
fee_notes: FMM tourist permit fee applies (~$57 USD); length of stay granted is at the immigration officer's discretion, up to this maximum.

conditions_text: Without a qualifying US, UK, Canadian, Japanese, or Schengen visa/residence document, Indian nationals must obtain a Mexican visa in advance.

Indian nationals holding a valid multiple-entry US visa (or Canadian/Schengen) are exempt from needing a separate Costa Rican visa. Authorized stay cannot exceed the remaining validity of that US visa.
fee_notes: Initial stamp is typically 30 days; extendable to a total of 90 days from within Costa Rica.

conditions_text: Indian passport alone falls into Costa Rica's restricted-visa group; without a qualifying US/Canada/Schengen document, a visa must be approved in advance.
Georgia grants visa-free entry to holders of a valid visa or residence permit from the US, UK, Japan, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Israel, South Korea, Ireland, Schengen, or GCC countries.
Indian passport holders without a qualifying third-country visa can apply for Georgia's standard e-visa.
fee_notes: Paid e-visa, applied for online.

conditions_text: Armenia grants visa on arrival to holders of a valid visa or residence permit from the US, EU/Schengen, UK, Australia, Canada, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, or Russia.
Indian nationals without a qualifying third-country visa can apply for Armenia's standard e-visa.
A valid US, UK, EU, or Schengen visa or residence permit substitutes for a Serbian visa entirely, for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
Without a qualifying third-country visa, Indian nationals can apply for Serbia's e-visa for the same 90-day allowance.
Since 19 May 2025, all Indian nationals get a non-extendable 14-day visa-free stay in the Philippines for tourism, with no other visa required.
Indian nationals who also hold a valid US (or Australia/Canada/Japan/Schengen/Singapore/UK) visa or resident visa get 30 days visa-free instead of the standard 14.
A valid US visa with at least 180 days' remaining validity (excluding C1 transit visas) substitutes for a Colombian visa for tourism.
Without a qualifying US or Schengen visa, Indian nationals must apply for Colombia's online visitor visa in advance.
Indian nationals holding a valid US, UK, Canada, Australia, or Schengen visa or permanent resident permit (minimum 6 months' validity) can stay visa-free for tourism or business.
fee_notes: Up to 180 days within any 365-day period.

conditions_text: Without a qualifying US/UK/Canada/Australia/Schengen document, Indian nationals must obtain a Peruvian visa in advance.
Indian passport holders can get an e-Visa on Arrival for Indonesia (including Bali), independent of any other visa held.
fee_notes: IDR 500,000 (~$32), paid on arrival or pre-purchased online; one extension is usually possible.

conditions_text: The Maldives grants visa-free entry on arrival to virtually all nationalities. Indian nationals specifically get 90 days (most nationalities get 30) under a bilateral reciprocity arrangement.

Sri Lanka requires an ETA (Electronic Travel Authorization) for Indian nationals, applied for online at eta.gov.lk. Since 25 May 2026 the ETA is free of charge for Indian passport holders, with double-entry allowed within the validity window.
fee_notes: Free as of 25 May 2026 (previously ~$20 USD). Extendable up to a total of 270 days from within Sri Lanka.

German passport holders are on Armenia's unilateral visa-exemption list and may enter for tourism, business, or family visits without a visa. Stay is capped at 180 days per calendar year, and longer stays or employment require a residence application before that period expires.

German citizens do not need a visa for purely touristic stays in Colombia; immigration stamps an initial permitted stay of up to 90 days on arrival, which can be extended once by a further 90 days at Migración Colombia's discretion. Travelers must also complete the free online Check-Mig pre-registration within 72 hours before each flight.

German citizens do not need a visa for tourist entry to Costa Rica and may be granted up to 180 days on arrival, though immigration officers can grant a shorter period based on return ticket, funds, and stated purpose. A passport valid at least 6 months beyond the stay and proof of onward travel are required.

German citizens may enter and stay in Georgia for up to 360 days without a visa; a residence permit must be obtained at a Public Service Hall before this period expires for longer stays. Since 1 January 2026, entrants must also show proof of health/travel insurance covering the whole stay with minimum coverage of 30,000 GEL.

German citizens can obtain a paid visa-on-arrival (or the equivalent electronic e-VOA applied for online in advance) at Indonesian entry points for tourism, valid up to 30 days with one 30-day extension available online. A passport valid at least 6 months and a return/onward ticket are required; volunteer or paid work is not permitted on this visa.
fee_notes: IDR 500,000 paid in cash at the airport, or paid online in advance for the electronic version (e-VOA).

conditions_text: German tourists receive a free 30-day visa on arrival in the Maldives after completing the mandatory IMUGA online entry declaration within 96 hours before arrival. An extension to a total of 90 days is possible but must be applied for locally and requires a recommendation from the resort/hotel.
fee_notes: Free for the initial 30-day visa on arrival; extension to 90 days is a separate paid, in-country application.

conditions_text: German citizens do not need a visa for tourism, transit, or business (without taking up employment) in Mexico as long as the stay does not exceed 180 days; the actual number of days granted is set by the immigration officer at entry and stamped in the passport (or noted on the FMM tourist card).

German citizens do not need a visa for tourist stays in Peru of up to 90 days per half-year; the exact permitted duration is not guaranteed to be the full 90 days and depends on information given at entry. Overstaying incurs a fine of 5 Peruvian soles per day before departure.

German tourists receive a fee-free 30-day visa waiver on arrival in the Philippines upon presenting a valid return or onward flight ticket; a further extension to a maximum of 59 total days is possible through the Bureau of Immigration. Pre-arrival online registration via the government's eTravel portal (etravel.gov.ph) is required, producing a QR code that airlines check at check-in.

German citizens do not need a visa for tourist entry to Serbia and may stay up to 90 days within any 180-day period; time spent in Kosovo counts toward this same 90-day limit under Serbian rules. Longer stays or employment require a residence permit applied for in advance or after arrival at the local foreign police office.

German citizens must obtain an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) before traveling to Sri Lanka via the official eta.gov.lk portal; it is issued as a single-entry tourist authorization for an initial 30 days. Since 25 May 2026 the tourist ETA is free of charge for German nationals (previously a paid category); extensions are described as extremely time-consuming and should be arranged with the Department of Immigration and Emigration in advance.
fee_notes: Free of charge for German citizens as of 25 May 2026 (a change from the earlier USD 50 fee).

conditions_text: German citizens do not need a visa for entry and stay in Turkey of up to 90 days within any 180-day period. The previous practice of leaving for a single day to reset a new 90-day period is no longer permitted, and visa-free entry does not guarantee an absolute right of admission.

German citizens holding a valid biometric passport do not need a visa for tourism, business (without taking up employment), or visit purposes in the UAE, for up to 90 days within any 180-day period. The passport must be valid for at least six months from the date of entry.
Singaporeans may enter Armenia visa-free for short stays of up to 180 days from the date of initial entry within a 12-month period.
Singaporeans can visit Colombia for up to 90 days for tourism without a visa.
Singaporeans can visit Costa Rica for up to 180 days without a visa for tourism; the exact length of stay granted is determined by the immigration officer (Migración) on arrival.
Citizens and stateless persons permanently residing in Singapore may enter and stay in Georgia without a visa for up to one full year (365 days) per entry.
Singapore passport holders may enter Indonesia visa-free for tourism under the A1 Visa Exemption for up to 30 days; this visa-free stay cannot be extended.
Singaporeans receive a free visa on arrival for up to 30 days, provided they hold an onward/return ticket and proof of sufficient funds or a confirmed accommodation booking.
fee_notes: Free of charge for the initial 30 days; can be extended for up to a total of 90 days for a fee (approx. 750 MVR for the extension).

conditions_text: Singaporeans can visit Mexico for up to 180 days without a visa, provided no employment is pursued during the stay.
Singaporeans can visit Peru for tourism for up to 90 days without a visa.

Singapore passport holders may enter the Philippines visa-free for up to 30 days for tourism, provided they hold a return/onward ticket and a passport valid at least 6 months beyond the intended stay; longer stays require an extension from the Bureau of Immigration.
Singaporeans can visit Serbia for up to 90 days within a 180-day period from the date of initial entry, without a visa.

Under a bilateral reciprocal agreement between Sri Lanka and Singapore, Singapore nationals must obtain an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) before arrival, valid for 30 days with double-entry from the date of first arrival.
fee_notes: ETA is processed free of charge for Singapore nationals under the reciprocal agreement (in effect since 25 May 2026); extensions beyond 30 days require payment of the applicable visa fee.

conditions_text: Singapore passport holders do not require a visa for visits of less than 90 days within any 180-day period to Türkiye for social/tourist visit purposes.
Singapore passport holders can stay visa-free for up to 90 days in the UAE within a 180-day period, with entry stamped on arrival and no advance visa application needed.
Brazilian passport holders may enter Armenia without a visa for stays of up to 180 days, one of the more generous visa-free allowances Armenia grants to any nationality.

Brazilian nationals do not need a visa for tourism, business, or transit; a Permiso de Turismo (PT) of up to 90 days is granted on arrival, and a valid Brazilian national ID card can substitute for a passport under the CAN/Mercosur framework.
Brazil is classified in Group 1 of Costa Rica's official visa directive (Directrices Generales de Visas), which allows entry without a visa for up to 180 calendar days, generally non-extendable.
Brazil is on Georgia's official visa-exemption list, and Brazilian passport holders may enter and remain in Georgia for up to 365 days without a visa.

Since 3 July 2025, under Minister of Immigration and Corrections Regulation No. 9 of 2025, Brazilian citizens can enter Indonesia visa-free for tourism for up to 30 days. An electronic Visa on Arrival (e-VOA) remains available as an alternative and can be extended once for a further 30 days.
fee_notes: Free under the visa-exemption route; the alternative e-VOA costs about IDR 500,000 (roughly USD 32) if chosen instead.

conditions_text: Brazilian passport holders receive a free 30-day tourist visa on arrival, provided they show proof of onward travel, prepaid accommodation, and sufficient funds, plus complete the online IMUGA Traveller Declaration before arrival.
fee_notes: Free of charge on arrival; extensions of up to a further 60 days (90 total) are possible for a fee.

conditions_text: As of 5 February 2026, Mexico requires Brazilian nationals to hold a visa. A new fully-online electronic visa (visa electrónica) is available for a single entry by air only, for visitors not engaging in paid activities; it does not replace the traditional consular visa, which remains required for land/sea entry or multiple entries.
fee_notes: Traditional multi-entry consular visitor visa costs about USD 56 (2026 rate) and is valid up to 180 days; the electronic visa's fee and exact authorized stay were not specified in the official announcement.

conditions_text: As a Mercosur-associated nationality, Brazilian citizens can enter Peru without a visa for tourism; total stay as a visa-exempt tourist is capped at 183 cumulative days within any rolling 365-day period, under Legislative Decree No. 1350 (Migration Law).

Under a bilateral exchange of notes between the Philippines and Brazil on reciprocal abolition of non-immigrant visa requirements, Brazilian passport holders may enter and stay in the Philippines visa-free for 59 days — longer than the standard 30-day allowance most nationalities receive.
Brazilian ordinary passport holders do not need a visa for tourism or business and may stay up to 90 days within any 6-month period counted from the date of first entry.

Since October 2025, Sri Lanka requires all visitors, including Brazilians, to obtain an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) online before departure. Brazil is not among the roughly 40 nationalities granted the ETA free of charge, so the standard fee applies; the ETA permits a 30-day stay.
fee_notes: Standard ETA fee of approximately USD 50, paid online at the official eta.gov.lk portal.

conditions_text: Brazilian passport holders may enter Turkey without a visa for tourism or business, for up to 90 days within any 180-day period, under a visa-exemption arrangement in place since 2004.

Under a bilateral visa-waiver agreement in force since July 2018, Brazilian ordinary, official, and diplomatic passport holders may enter the UAE without a visa and stay up to 90 days within any 12-month period.
